'''Satakunari Shrine''' (狭田国生神社, *Satakunari Jinja*<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 58</ref>) is an [[auxiliary shrine]] (*sessha*) of [[Ise Grand Shrine]] ({{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, *Naikū*), located on the left bank of the Sotojida River in {{ill|Tamaki|en|Tamaki|qid=Q1289593|lt=Tamaki}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}, Japan. Locally, it is affectionately referred to as "Haiko-san."<ref name="tm4">Kaneko (1984): p. 34</ref>
== Overview ==
It is one of the 13 auxiliary shrines in Tamaki Town.<ref name="sk4">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p.204</ref><ref name="ic"/> Among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, it Ranks 26th.<ref name="uy"/>
The name "Sata" is presumed to derive from its location, "Sada."<ref name="sk4"/> The local nickname "Haiko" is thought to be a variation of the enshrined deity Hayakawahiko no Mikoto.<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p.205</ref> In "Seyō Gorin Ikkyō," it is noted that "commonly referred to as Haiko Shrine, the area is also known as 'Samukawa Shrine.'"<ref name="tm5">Kaneko (1984): p.35</ref>
It is believed to have been established by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}.<ref name="ic"/> The shrine grounds cover 1,656 square meters.<ref name="sk5"/> The shrine building, constructed in the Shinmei-zukuri style with wooden planks, faces south and is enclosed by a single layer of tamagaki (sacred fence).<ref name="sk5"/> There is no offertory box.
== Enshrined Deities ==
The shrine enshrines three deities: Hayakawahiko no Mikoto and Hayakawahime no Mikoto, gods of the Sotojōda River flowing nearby, and Yamazue no Mitama, the guardian deity of the land.<ref name="ic"/> The "Kōtai Jingū Gishikichō" already mentions the enshrinement of these three deities, with "Hayakawa" referring to the Sotojōda River.<ref name="sk5"/> The parent deities of Hayakawahiko and Hayakawahime are enshrined at {{ill|Sugihara Shrine|ja|棒原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugihara Shrine|qq=}}.<ref name="sk5"/>
== History ==
According to the "Yamato-hime-no-mikoto Seiki," the shrine was established when Yamato-hime-no-mikoto, upon crossing a stream with Amaterasu Ōmikami, received an offering of sacred rice paddies from Hayakawa Hiko no Mikoto, leading to the shrine's foundation as "Hayakawa Sata Shrine."<ref name="sk4"/> In ancient times, the shrine had priests appointed by the Ōmiya family, who conducted daily rituals.<ref name="sk5"/>
The shrine fell into disrepair during the Sengoku period but was restored in 1663 (Kanbun 3) with the efforts of Ōmiya priest Kawabe Masanaga.<ref>Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): pp.204-205</ref> The shrine was rebuilt in January 1915 (Taisho 4),<ref name="uy">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): p.11</ref> reconstructed in November 1956 (Showa 31), and repaired in June 1979 (Showa 54).<ref name="sk5"/>
== Festivals ==
Local leaders visit the shrine annually on January 17.<ref name="ic"/> The shrine holds Inari Festival (February 20), Tsukinami Festival (June 20 and December 20), and Niiname Festival (November 27) in the style of the Inner Shrine's pilgrimage rituals.<ref name="sk5"/>
== Flora ==
Camellias planted within the shrine grounds bloom in spring.<ref name="ic"/>
== Access ==
;Public Transport
* About 500 meters northeast of JR Sangu Line's Tamaki Station.<ref name="sk4"/>
* Just south of the Kayamachi bus stop on Mie Kotsu buses.<ref name="sk4"/>
;By Car
* About 6 minutes (3.7 km) north from Tamaki IC on the Ise Expressway via Mie Prefectural Route 530 (Sunny Road), along Mie Prefectural Route 717.<ref name="sk4"/> There is no parking available nearby.
